sourcePages: PDF pages 13-28 (booklet pages 5-20); scheme of studies PDF pages 23-27 (booklet pages 15-19)
scope: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) is a four-year undergraduate degree at NQF Level 6 that builds a strong foundation in business and management principles and integrates theoretical knowledge with practical application for a dynamic, competitive global business environment. The curriculum spans general education, core business areas including accounting, finance, marketing and human resource management, interdisciplinary courses, specialization electives, an internship and a capstone project. Emphasis is placed on analytical thinking, problem solving, ethical decision-making, leadership and an entrepreneurial mindset. Graduates are prepared for entry-level managerial roles in public and private sector organisations, for starting or expanding family businesses, or for advanced study in business and management.
duration: 4 years (8 regular semesters); maximum 6 years (12 regular semesters), further extendible by 1 year (2 regular semesters) with the permission of the statutory bodies

eligibility: Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC), A-levels, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the IBCC, involving 12 years of schooling with a minimum of 50% marks.

Students admitted through lateral entry with Level 5 qualifications (for example non-relevant Associate Degrees, BA, BSc or B.Com) must complete a bridging semester of 15-18 credit hours of deficiency courses determined by the HEI, offered as a complete set in one semester.
No bridging semester is required for holders of relevant Associate Degrees completed under the semester system.
passingCriteria: Completion of 130 credit hours in a minimum of eight semesters spread over a minimum of four years.
CGPA of at least 2.00 out of 4.00 at completion of the degree; the university may set a higher standard.
Completion of the 3-credit-hour internship or field experience and the capstone project, neither of which may be substituted by other coursework.

Completion of relevant business and management certification equivalent to 3 credit hours in total over the four-year program, where 16 hours of study count as 1 credit hour; the department guides the choice of certifications.
internship: A field experience or internship of 3 credit hours is a mandatory, non-substitutable requirement of the BBA degree. It lasts six to eight weeks, is preferably undertaken during a semester break or summer, and must be formally evaluated by a faculty member in consultation with the field supervisor. The scheme lists it in Semester VIII, and students may complete it any time after the fifth semester.
projects: A capstone project, typically spanning three to six credit hours (3 credit hours in the program structure and scheme), is a mandatory requirement of the BBA degree. It must be supervised and graded by a faculty member in accordance with the HEI's protocols and cannot be substituted with additional coursework or the internship. It is placed in Semester VIII.
notes: The document calls the scheme of studies 'suggestive'; HEIs may redistribute courses across semesters based on staff and facilities. Course load is 15-21 credit hours per regular semester (16-18 weeks including 1-2 weeks of examinations); up to 8 credit hours may be offered in summer/winter semesters for failure, repetition or deficiency courses.

Credit notation in the schemes is theory+practical (e.g. '3+0', '2+1'); the Internship/Field Experience row gives only '3'. Semester totals are stated in the document and were verified by addition; they sum to 130.

Discipline-related/Major courses total 78 credit hours (26 courses): mandatory core 33 + HEI-decided core 27 + specialization electives 18. With General Education 34, interdisciplinary 12, internship 3 and capstone 3 the minimum is 130.

Mandatory core (33 credit hours, 11 courses) is chosen by category from PDF page 17 (booklet 9): Management 9 cr (3 of Principles of Management, Organizational Behavior, Human Resource Management, Strategic Management); Marketing 6 cr (2 of Principles of Marketing, Marketing Management, Digital Marketing); Finance 6 cr (2 of Business Finance, Financial Management, Islamic Finance); Accounting 6 cr (2 of Principles of Accounting, Managerial Accounting/Cost Accounting, Financial Accounting); Others 6 cr (2 of Business Research Methods, AI in Business, Digital Transformation and Innovation). The five courses not selected move to the HEI-decided core pool. The scheme's 11 'Major' courses are Principles of Management, Organizational Behaviour, Principles of Accounting, Financial Accounting, Business Finance, Principles of Marketing, Marketing Management, Financial Management, Human Resource Management, Business Research Methods and AI in Business.

HEI-decided core courses (27 credit hours, 9 courses): the document gives a suggestive list of 27 subjects (PDF pages 17-18, booklet 9-10), e.g. Business Analytics, Business Communication, Business Ethics, Business Law, Business Math and Stats, Corporate Finance, E-Commerce and Digital Business, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Management Information System, Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Total Quality Management; HEIs may add courses with statutory approval. HEI Decided Core Course-VIII in Semester VII is earmarked for a business and management relevant certification.

Interdisciplinary courses (minimum 12 credit hours, 4 courses) are chosen from five clusters on PDF pages 22-23 (booklet 14-15): AI & Technology, Economics, Law, Sustainability, and Others; students may take at most one course from a cluster.

Specialization rule (section 1.5.6): six electives (18 credit hours) taken from a single cluster allow the specialization to be noted on the transcript; electives taken across clusters give no specialization; specializations are never printed on the degree certificate. The listed clusters are not exhaustive and HEIs may add clusters with statutory approval. Section 1.7.1: effective Fall 2026 all BBA programs bearing specialization-related captions/titles (e.g. 'BBA in Sales and Marketing') must be discontinued.

Source oddity: the cluster headed '1.5.6.9 Project Management' (PDF page 22, booklet 14) actually lists sustainability-themed courses (Business Ethics and Governance, Circular Economy and Business Models, Climate Change and Business Strategy, Corporate Social Responsibility, Environmental Economics, Green Marketing and Branding, Social Impact Assessment, Sustainability Reporting and ESG Metrics), and a stray '1.' precedes the heading; the heading is kept as printed. The Human Resource Management cluster list also has duplicated letters (a, b) in the source.

Fehm-e-Quran appears in the General Education table as one 2-credit-hour course but is delivered in the scheme as two 0+1 parts (Semesters II and III) for Muslim students; for non-Muslim students HEIs may replace the 2 credit hours with a suitable General Education course approved by their statutory bodies. 'Organizational Behaviour' is the spelling used in the scheme; the core-course table uses 'Organizational Behavior'.
Section 1.7.2: the BBA is not deemed equivalent to any other Level 6 qualification, including BS programs in specialized areas of business or management.

Section 1.7.4 (PDF page 28, booklet 20): 'Students enrolled in the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) shall be allowed to exit the program with an Associate Degree in Business Administration, provided they have completed the requirements of the Associate Degree in the first four semesters as per HEC Undergraduate Education Policy 2023.' The first four semesters of the BBA scheme total 70 credit hours (18+18+16+18).

Lateral entry (section 1.7.3): transcripts of lateral-entry students show only post-admission coursework plus the prior qualification's credit hours (exact number for Associate Degrees; '50 credit hours earned against BA/BSc/B.Com as per National Qualifications Framework' for conventional degrees); bridging-semester grades are listed but excluded from the CGPA.

Accreditation: the document names the National Business Education Accreditation Council (NBEAC) as the accreditation council that contributed to the curriculum (PDF page 9) and whose No Objection Certificate is required for new BS titles (PDF page 31); it does not contain an explicit sentence stating that NBEAC accredits the BBA.
The document supersedes the 2012 Business Administration curriculum and the 2019 Revised Business Education Curriculum notification to the extent of inconsistency (PDF page 11, booklet 3).

scope: The two-year Associate Degree in business and management disciplines is an NQF Level 5 undergraduate program for students who have completed 12 years of schooling. It provides foundational knowledge and practical skills in business and management functions, preparing graduates for entry-level, para-professional positions across businesses and industries, or for further study through lateral entry into a four-year bachelor's degree. The curriculum balances general education with discipline-specific courses and combines theoretical understanding with applied learning. In this program the thematic area is Business Administration, the title the document assigns to the exit award for BBA students who complete the Associate Degree requirements in the first four semesters.

notes: The document gives its own Associate Degree scheme of studies (section 6.4.4, PDF pages 69-70, booklet 61-62), which is used here; the AD is not defined as the first four semesters of the BBA or BS scheme, although both the BBA (section 1.7.4) and BS (section 2.9.2) sections allow students to exit with an Associate Degree after completing its requirements in the first four semesters.

Thematic areas: section 6.2 (PDF page 65, booklet 57) states that all NQF Level 5 programs in the discipline must be titled 'Associate Degree in (thematic area of business and management)' and lists the NCRC-decided areas as Accounting, Marketing, Finance, Human Resource Management, Entrepreneurship, Supply Chain Management, Islamic Banking and Finance, Project Management, Business Analytics and Digital Marketing. 'Business Administration' is not in that list.

Basis for the 'Business Administration' title: section 1.7.4 (PDF page 28, booklet 20) reads: 'Students enrolled in the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) shall be allowed to exit the program with an Associate Degree in Business Administration, provided they have completed the requirements of the Associate Degree in the first four semesters as per HEC Undergraduate Education Policy 2023.' The first four semesters of the BBA scheme total 70 credit hours (18+18+16+18).

Mandatory core (15 credit hours) comprises Principles of Management, Organizational Behavior, Principles of Marketing, Business Finance and Principles of Accounting (section 6.4.2, PDF page 68, booklet 60); all five appear as 'Major' in the scheme.

Domain courses: the structure table calls the 21 credit hours 'Domain Specific Courses wherein the Associate Degree is offered (to be decided by HEIs)', while the scheme labels them 'HEI Decided Core Course-I' to '-VII' (7 courses of 3 credit hours each); titles are kept as printed. The document gives no domain course list for any thematic area.

The scheme totals 70 credit hours (18+18+16+18); the structure permits 70-72. Stated semester totals were verified by addition. Course load is 15-21 credit hours per regular semester, with up to 8 credit hours in summer/winter semesters for failure, repetition or deficiency courses.

No degree award requirements section, CGPA threshold, internship or capstone project is given for the Associate Degree in the document; passingCriteria are derived from the program structure table (section 6.4) and 'internship' and 'projects' are null. The document says the AD follows the HEC Undergraduate Education Policy 2023 and subsequent notifications.

Fehm-e-Quran is one 2-credit-hour General Education course delivered as two 0+1 parts (Semesters II and III) for Muslim students; HEIs may substitute a suitable General Education course for non-Muslim students.

Section 6.1 notes that the AD serves as a route to four-year degrees through lateral entry; under BBA section 1.7.3 holders of relevant Associate Degrees completed under the semester system need no bridging semester.
Accreditation: the document names NBEAC as the accreditation council involved in the curriculum but does not explicitly state that NBEAC accredits Associate Degrees.
